exhibits.title: The long-necked giant
exhibits.subject: Mamenchisaurus
exhibits.brief: A long, largely horizontal sauropod mount. Two separated support islands leave a 7 m cross-passage through the reserved bay. Keep the passage clear above 2.8 m; validate the final neck, tail and supports before installation.

exhibits.title: Predator in motion
exhibits.subject: Tarbosaurus
exhibits.brief: A tall theropod mount, read from the connecting walk and the north overlook. Orient the long axis along Z. Reserve the full tail sweep inside the envelope.

exhibits.title: Built for defence
exhibits.subject: Armoured dinosaur
exhibits.brief: Armour, tail mechanics and defensive body plans. No moving parts are supplied; use a separate animation clip later.

exhibits.title: Small dinosaur, big story
exhibits.subject: Protoceratops
exhibits.brief: A family-scale mount with a lower reading rail. Its envelope intentionally leaves the dinosaur entrance unobstructed.

exhibits.title: Footprints as evidence
exhibits.subject: Trackway casting
exhibits.brief: A shallow, accessible examination surface for a trackway cast. The display table is already built; add only the geological exhibit.

exhibits.title: Teeth tell a story
exhibits.subject: Comparative teeth
exhibits.brief: A side-facing cabinet above the ramp. Compare feeding adaptations using original tooth models. Keep all geometry inside the shallow case.

exhibits.title: After the dinosaurs
exhibits.subject: Australian megafauna
exhibits.brief: Reserve for a Diprotodon or another Australian megafaunal subject. Label its different time period explicitly; do not call every prehistoric animal a dinosaur.

exhibits.title: A different kind of flight
exhibits.subject: Pterosaur
exhibits.brief: Suspended pterosaur allowance. It is not a dinosaur. Model rigging separately, check supports against roof ribs, and keep the entire envelope above visitor head height.

exhibits.title: Reading deep time
exhibits.subject: Fossil comparison
exhibits.brief: An overlook-level comparison table. The shell includes the table and guardrails; add fossil specimens only.

exhibits.title: A wall of wings
exhibits.subject: Butterfly diversity
exhibits.brief: Pinned-specimen composition in a shallow wall cabinet. Use separate small models, or an original baked specimen atlas for distant views. No specimen artwork is supplied.

exhibits.title: The beetle collection
exhibits.subject: Beetle diversity
exhibits.brief: A second framed collection wall with warm conservation-style presentation. Design allowances are not real conservation specifications.

exhibits.title: Record breakers
exhibits.subject: Insect Hall of Fame theme
exhibits.brief: An island vitrine for insect superlatives. Confirm any eventual largest/heaviest/longest claim with a species-specific source before adding final labels.

exhibits.title: Six legs, many lives
exhibits.subject: Insect classification
exhibits.brief: Low comparison table for body plan models. Deliberately separate insect classification from the eight-legged gallery next door.

exhibits.title: A city in the leaves
exhibits.subject: Green tree ant colony
exhibits.brief: Empty habitat enclosure. You will supply nest, branches, substrate, ant meshes and animation. This is not a live-animal husbandry design.

exhibits.title: The patient hunter
exhibits.subject: Mantid habitat
exhibits.brief: Wall-side enclosure reserved for mantid, branches and foliage. No placeholder insects or greenery are included.

exhibits.title: Life below the surface
exhibits.subject: Aquatic invertebrates
exhibits.brief: An aquarium-format shell with a dry, empty interior. Add water and invertebrates later; avoid nested transmissive surfaces in the final GLB.

exhibits.title: Nature’s recyclers
exhibits.subject: Decomposer habitat
exhibits.brief: An empty ecological exhibit for leaf litter and decomposer invertebrates. Habitat dressing remains part of your Blender stage.

exhibits.title: Anatomy, enlarged
exhibits.subject: Insect body systems
exhibits.brief: A deliberately enlarged anatomical model. Display its scale multiplier on the future label so visitors do not confuse model size with animal size.

exhibits.title: Tools for feeding
exhibits.subject: Insect mouthparts
exhibits.brief: Enlarged comparative mouthparts inside an island vitrine. Include chewing, piercing or other forms only after choosing referenced species.

exhibits.title: A life transformed
exhibits.subject: Life cycles
exhibits.brief: A chronological specimen sequence. The cabinet and typography frame are present; model the lifecycle stages in Blender.

exhibits.title: Small but essential
exhibits.subject: Pollination
exhibits.brief: A teaching-table allowance for insect–flower relationships. Flowers and insects are both intentionally omitted.

exhibits.title: Beyond six legs
exhibits.subject: Arachnid comparison
exhibits.brief: A comparison vitrine introducing arachnids. Use accurate leg counts and label specimens independently from insects.

exhibits.title: Behind the glass
exhibits.subject: Tarantula enclosure
exhibits.brief: An empty quarantine-themed enclosure. No fictional biosecurity system is presented as a working or legally compliant facility.

exhibits.title: Our backyard neighbours
exhibits.subject: Local spider enclosure
exhibits.brief: An enclosure for a chosen locally occurring spider. Final species, location and safety interpretation must be researched before publication.

exhibits.title: Architecture of silk
exhibits.subject: Web structures
exhibits.brief: A backlit web-study cabinet. Supply the silk geometry or baked transparent texture; keep the future exhibit readable without bloom.

exhibits.title: The last giants
exhibits.subject: Triceratops
exhibits.brief: The feature-gallery mount with a full walk-around route. Inspired by the idea of Melbourne’s Triceratops gallery; this is not a model or reproduction of Horridus.

exhibits.title: Evidence in the rock
exhibits.subject: Fossil preparation
exhibits.brief: A wall-case allowance for preparation tools, rock matrix and fossil evidence. All these assets are left for Blender.

exhibits.title: The discovery bench
exhibits.subject: Handling collection
exhibits.brief: A school-group table for tactile or digital models. The runtime interaction is a readable design card, not a finished scientific activity.

exhibits.title: Make an observation
exhibits.subject: Microscope station
exhibits.brief: Reserve for microscope and specimen-tray assets. Do not export room furniture with the specimen GLB.

exhibits.title: A future living centre
exhibits.subject: Botanical installation
exhibits.brief: An empty central planting bed. Trees, ferns, ground cover and fauna are excluded from this delivery. This is a quiet light-court interpretation, not the real Forest Gallery.
